regions: the massif's front (north of the Brackens)
about: The Frostline and the massif: an alpine cirque above the valley, crag over boulder faces, fir in the hollow, short turf and scree on the benches, a tarn, snow and a glacier on the top tiers. The cliff core's 'highland' biome and edge set (scripts/art/cliff_core.py) are the start; this brief adds what the Frostline needs on top of them, as data, for the kit owner (rules-system.md 4: the Frostline is the contrasting test region, built end to end on kit v1). Every family is a house ramp. 'kit' is pinned when kit v1 exists.
palette_intent: Cool and clear above the valley: grey-blue crag (crag_cool, crag) with warm crag bands catching the light, fresh green turf going cooler and sparser with height, near-black fir, white-blue snow and pale blue ice. The tarn is the one deep blue. Warmth comes only from lit rock bands, the hut's timber and small clusters of alpine flowers.

cliff_core.keep: the boulder faces in absolute-height bands, the clean turf lip, the stony foot with scree, rock steps between boulder cheeks, brooks in a small earth bank
add: snow_z: the snow line by tier (below)
falls > 0 where the Sleepwater crosses a face
trees: fir only, in the hollow and on the lowest benches

by_tier.recipe: alpine meadow: turf in broad patches, flower clusters, fir thinning upward, scree fans at the foot of faces
fir floor: needle litter on earth_cool, moss cushions, ferns along the stream
short cool turf, boulders in clusters, snow patches only in north-facing hollows (the cell north of a rim)
scree and turf in patches, cairns on the path
snow with blue ice where it steepens; crevasses as dark-blue slots on the grid; never walked off the trod

snow_line.corners: snow_corner pieces on north-facing rims from tier 4

ground.calm: as SB-05: snow and ice are the calmest grounds in the world, two tones and the odd lit drift edge; turf despeckled; scree is clusters of 2 or more texels, never single pixels

plants.where: Fir Hollow and the lowest benches, thinning upward; none above the cirque floor
the step and cirque floor rims, in twos and threes
scree edges on the high bench
the hollow's stream and the foot of shady faces
boulder tops and the fir floor
small clumps on the benches and cirque floor (gentian blue, saxifrage white, rock-rose yellow), never spread thin

clusters.where: the cirque floor and the High Fells' obstacle field; 800 px apart (benchmark 9)
the hollow and benches, a clearing kept round the cabin
at the foot of a crag face, fanning downhill
the Col Path's bends and the High Fells
Snowmelt Lake's shore, not on the outlet

tiers.notes: the woodland has only 32 px: the Frostline adds 12 and 16 px rock steps on the benches and 40 px crag faces on the cirque headwall and the glacier's front (rules-system.md 4, the golden's gaps)

edges.from_woodland: Rock, not earth: boulder faces in bands fixed in absolute height, so one band runs through every face of the region; a clean turf lip one or two texels over, lit along its top; a stony foot with scree. Above the snow line the lip is a snow cornice (the cliff core's snow corner). Volume (to-all-volume): faces step in and out by whole cells as buttresses and gullies, lit top-left planes, crisp cast shadows on snow.
edges.stair: rock steps cut between boulder cheeks (cliff core 'rock'), on north-south legs only
edges.bank: small earth bank on the brooks; the tarn's shore is boulders and turf, no reeds; ice edges on the glacier's melt pools

water.notes: Snowmelt Lake is the Sleepwater's source; the stream falls where it crosses each face (falls with plunge pools, cliff core NEUTRAL 'fall'), runs through Fir Hollow and leaves over the escarpment into the woodland's spring pool

animals: ibex on the scree and moraine
ambience.light: colder and brighter than the valley: snow lifts the shadows a touch; dusk turns the snow warm (snow_warm) for a short time

transitions.where: the escarpment above the woodland's spring pool
transitions.how: fir thins into broadleaf on the valley side; the falls cross the line

transitions.where: the Col hut and the benches
transitions.how: alpine meadow shares the turf families; flowers and fir mark the highland side
